How Did Arab Parties Get So Strong in Israel? In just one week, Benjamin Netanyahu’s world shifted. On 27 October, his bloc fell to 53 seats in Israel’s election, short of the 61 needed to govern. On 3 November, his closest ally’s party lost both houses of the US Congress, and Vice President JD Vance named the Iran war and Washington’s relationship with Israel among the reasons.
Now the key to power in Israel lies with the people Netanyahu spent the campaign warning against: Israel’s Arab-led parties, which won a record 19 seats on the back of historic turnout.
